clue.text: Support provided in jolly surroundings

indicators.note: the word for jolly forms the surroundings, enclosing the word for provided

parts.note: jolly is British informal for very, as in jolly good
provided means if, as a condition

explanation.surface: Someone backs a cause, so long as the atmosphere around them is cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is British informal for 'very', as in 'jolly good', and 'surroundings' wraps it round the condition word.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify a claim is to back it up with proof, so support works as a synonym.

clue.text: After holiday, worker is unemployed

indicators.note: the worker comes after the holiday, so its letters follow

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Back from a break, an employee finds the job has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vac' is British student slang for the long university holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A post that is vacant is unfilled, and a vacant person may be idle, without employment.

clue.text: Organise a game of golf, using under- ARTI hand tactics

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Organise a game of golf, using under- ARTI hand tactics': OCR garble splits the definition (underhand tactics) with stray 'ARTI'; scan crop is blank and a search found no copy. Parse would be RUN + A + ROUND.
annotationWithheld.clue: Organise a game of golf, using under- ARTI hand tactics

clue.text: The truth about eastern view

indicators.note: the word for truth goes about, enclosing, the abbreviation for eastern

parts.note: the truth is a fact, something true

explanation.surface: Honesty concerning how people see the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one aspect of a matter, a particular way of looking at it, so view fits.

clue.text: Make a hole in case that's superlatively durable

parts.note: to stab is to pierce, making a hole
lest is an old word meaning in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: Punch a hole in a box that is the toughest going.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and lasting; the -est form is the superlative, the most durable.

clue.text: A bottle artisan cracked? He wouldn't do that

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman's bottle breaks, but this man would never drink from it anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' signals the anagram of A BOTTLE ARTISAN; 'that' points back to the surface's bottle, which a teetotaller would never open.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refuses alcohol altogether, so he would not crack open a bottle.

clue.text: Soundly stopped what 5 is on; every body wants to be on it

definitions.text: every body wants to be on it

indicators.note: soundly tells us the word for stopped is heard, not spelt

parts.note: something banned has been stopped or prohibited
a teetotaller is said to be on the wagon

explanation.surface: A trend that everyone wants to join, linked to the abstinence of an earlier clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' gives BAND from BANNED said aloud; 5-down is TOTAL ABSTAINER, someone on the wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump on the bandwagon is to join a popular movement, which everybody wants to be part of.

clue.text: School is said to be worried

indicators.note: is said tells us the school's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school has a reputation for anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is said' gives the homophone of ETON, the English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eaten up with worry is consumed by it, so eaten means worried or troubled.

clue.text: Charm beginning to tame wild animals

indicators.note: the beginning of the word tame is its first letter
wild means uncontrolled, so these letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A spell for starting to tame savage beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives T; 'wild' makes ALISMAN from ANIMALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to have magical power, a lucky charm.

clue.text: Facade with light plaster

parts.note: a light is a window, letting light into a building
a plaster is a wound dressing

explanation.surface: A building's front with a bright rendering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facade' and 'plaster' suggest building work, but the plaster is a sticking plaster for a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Window dressing is a display put on to impress, a misleading outward show or facade.

clue.text: One who hasn't volunteered to learn his words

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn
an actor's words are his script

explanation.surface: An actor drafted in against his will, just to memorise lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscript is someone compulsorily enlisted into the armed forces rather than a volunteer.

clue.text: Province at one time in the rear …

definitions.meaning: a former province of South Africa
an anatomical word for things relating to the buttocks, the nates

explanation.surface: A former territory lying at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is rare: from Latin nates, buttocks, so 'in the rear' is literally the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a former South African province and relating to the buttocks.

clue.text: … and not back in the front

indicators.note: back tells us those letters are read the other way round
in tells us the letters sit inside the word front

parts.note: the letters r, o, n sit in the middle of front

explanation.surface: The second half of a sentence about not being at the front either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks RON out of fRONt and 'back' turns it; the dots link the clue to the previous one's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor is a conjunction meaning and not, used to continue a negative.

clue.text: Game providing merry moments

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, merry
a wink is an instant, a moment

explanation.surface: A pastime giving cheerful instants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merry' is the British sense of tipsy, which TIDDLY also means.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddlywinks is a game of flicking small counters into a cup.

clue.text: When people were housebound, hardly any had dog at first

indicators.note: the dog comes at first, so its letters lead

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
few means hardly any

explanation.surface: In lockdown hardly anyone owned a dog early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housebound' points to lockdown, but a curfew is the older idea of a time after which nobody may go out.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is a time after which people must stay indoors, so they are confined to home.

clue.text: End lack of preparation for traditional measure

indicators.note: a preparation is something made up, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A call to stop being unready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparation' signals the anagram of END LACK OF; 'measure' is an old word for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an old word for a stately dance, and a folk dance is a traditional one.

clue.text: Flower, a big one, is out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A large bloom has opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' signals the anagram of A BIG ONE; it pretends the flower is in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A begonia is a garden plant grown for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Getting fine, villain at last going straight

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of villain

parts.note: arrowing means flying straight like an arrow

explanation.surface: A criminal finally reforms and does well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives N; 'going straight' suggests a reformed crook, but it means moving like an arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowing means becoming thinner, and fine means thin, so getting fine is narrowing.

clue.text: Labels showing spades and hearts

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: Tags marking card suits on a deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The card suits mislead: only spades is a suit here; hearts are tickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stickers are adhesive labels.

clue.text: Barber left a sovereign for child

parts.note: Sweeney Todd is the fictional demon barber of Fleet Street
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A hairdresser leaves a gold coin for a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The sovereign looks like the gold coin; it is a monarch, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a small child just learning to walk.

clue.text: Cockney's tough opponent returning to arctic plain

indicators.note: returning tells us the letters are read backwards
a Cockney drops his aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: a hard nut is a tough person, difficult to beat

explanation.surface: A hardened East Londoner's rival goes back to the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney's' drops the H to give ARDNUT and 'returning' reverses it. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless frozen plain of the Arctic regions.

clue.text: Brother officer's rough ride

parts.note: NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier's sibling has a bumpy journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is an untamed horse that gives a rider a wild, bucking ride.

clue.text: Families design backroom

parts.note: a clan is a group of related families
to destine something is to intend or design it for a purpose

explanation.surface: Family groups plan a back room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backroom' is an adjective here, as in backroom deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Backroom dealings are done in secret, out of sight, as clandestine ones are.

clue.text: Just not starting — that's terrible!

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: just means fair, lawful

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disgust at something barely unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops L from LAWFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very bad, so it is a synonym of terrible.

clue.text: It's no good leaving the country to find antelope

indicators.note: leaving means the letters go out of the country's name

parts.note: England is the country

explanation.surface: A ne'er-do-well emigrates to find wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes NG out of ENGLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Sweep voicing fear

indicators.note: voicing means saying aloud, so a word for fear is heard

parts.note: awe is reverential fear

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep says he is afraid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent AWE and OAR sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is a long oar used for rowing or steering a boat.

clue.text: Petite and charming female overwhelmed by turning current

indicators.note: the female letter is engulfed by the river
turning means the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: a river is a current; the Nile is the river

explanation.surface: A dainty woman swept away by a flowing stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes ELIN from NILE; 'overwhelmed by' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small and delicate with a fey charm, like an elf.

clue.text: Repeats develop into a rite

definitions.note: plural noun for a singular answer; the setter treats repeated doing as the act of repeating

indicators.note: to develop is to grow into a new form, so these letters change order

explanation.surface: Habits that grow into a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' signals the anagram of INTO A RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An iteration is a repetition of a process, so repeats describes it.

clue.text: Border of aquatic vegetation little eel burrows into without hesitation

indicators.note: the shortened eel digs inside the plant word

parts.note: sedge is a grassy plant of wet places

indicators.note: without means the hesitation is taken away

parts.note: an elver is a young eel
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: A young eel tunnels into waterside plants at a river's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: An elver is a young eel; 'without' drops the hesitation sound from it before 'burrows into' sinks it in the waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A selvedge is the woven edge of fabric that stops it fraying, a border.

clue.text: Girl meets soldier and love follows slowly

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
GI is an American soldier
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A young woman meets a soldier and romance slowly blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for playing slowly.
